item.title: CKBdapps 2.0：为 CKB 生态重新搭建的项目目录 (6 posts)
item.description: 提个想法，不一定靠谱： 是否有可能在这个 repo 中提供某种极简模式类似 awesome list 一样的东西？目前独立的网站和UI很酷，但对一小部分人来说（比如我），其实更想要的是类似 GitHub - aljazceru/awesome-nostr: nostr.net - awesome-nostr is a collection of projects and resources built on nostr to help developers and users find new things · GitHub 这样简单的东西就可以，一目了然，也有它的好处。我们可以有很酷的独立网站，但是否也可以顺便提供这样简洁明了的 aswsome list，用户也很容易提个 PR 请求收录自己的应用？ 谢谢 Retric 你的反馈，我们评估一下，应该是可以实现的。 Great work! item.title: Same lock script in Rust and in ckb-js-vm: 15k cycles vs 15M (3 posts)
item.description: Interesting benchmark, and the reproducible results are valuable. However, I think the main conclusion about startup overhead needs stronger experimental evidence. The 14.3M-cycle early-rejection case does not necessarily isolate VM startup and bytecode loading. It may also include runtime initialization, argument parsing, bindings, and other execution costs. Consequently, subtracting this value from the accepted-spend cycles does not rigorously establish that application logic accounts for only 5% of the total, or that JavaScript logic is approximately 66× more expensive than Rust. Similarly, attributing the additional 0.36M cycles entirely to 1.8 KB of extra bytecode is not justified...

item.title: Tranfr — Programmable Recovery for CKB (5 posts)
item.description: I am particularly concerned about the flow of cell capacity. In your current design, the args field might contain a significant amount of cell deadline data, which increases the minimum capacity required for a cell. However, for transactions involving only UDTs, the recipient could potentially claim the entire capacity without any restrictions. I would suggest reconsidering this aspect of the design. Especially for scenarios where the operator intends to transfer only UDTs, without any plan to transfer CKB. Thank you, I appreciate it. Good point on capacity. Right now the recipient takes the whole cell, so someone sending only UDTs would hand over the CKB deposit too. I see two fixes: (1)...

item.title: [DIS] Cellula on Fiber: a wallet, a checkout and an AI agent on a public mainnet LSP (7 posts)
item.description: Your past releases and activities show the significant effort poured into this mainnet-oriented product line. Best wishes! Honestly, this looks promising. Fiber needs more ways for regular users to actually use it, and having a wallet, merchant payments, and AI agent working together makes a lot of sense.
